QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_4

question.text: Saraswati PE Fund has paid-in capital of INR 1,000 crore. Cumulative distributions to LPs are INR 400 crore and the residual fair value of unrealised holdings is INR 1,100 crore. Compute DPI, RVPI and TVPI.

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Cumulative Distributions / PIC = 400/1000 = 0.40. RVPI = Residual Value / PIC = 1100/1000 = 1.10. TVPI = DPI + RVPI = 0.40 + 1.10 = 1.50. This matches the PDF Section 7.3.4.4 illustration verbatim. The Trap: Option A swaps numerators (distribution vs residual value). Option C subtracts instead of adding the two components. Option B sums everything into DPI incorrectly. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers DPI/RVPI/TVPI for all three AIF categories; XIX-A distributor exam uses them in client pitches; XXI-B PMS has no DPI/RVPI equivalent because PMS has no lock-up/commitment structure. Manager's Pro-Tip: TVPI > 1.0 alone is NOT proof of success — a TVPI of 1.50 with DPI 0.40 means 73% of reported value is still paper gains. LPAC investors discount RVPI-heavy TVPI heavily in secondary transfers.
